canonical_name: Structural stability of dynamical systems (exact object and proposition open)
literal_source_claim_zh: 系统在扰动下的稳定性
statement_blocker: The catalog does not specify the dynamical object, phase space, regularity, perturbation topology, equivalence relation, quantifier order, hypotheses, conclusion, or boundary cases. It also does not choose between a definition, robustness theorem, sufficient condition, characterization, classification, or existence statement. Selecting an Andronov-Pontryagin planar rough-system result, Peixoto's theorem, a Morse-Smale or Anosov structural-stability theorem, or a local hyperbolic-equilibrium theorem would invent or substitute mathematics.
domain_and_universes: Open: an accepted source must fix the dynamical object, time parameter, phase space or manifold, dimension, compactness and boundary conditions, differentiability class, topology on the system space, universe levels, and all required topological, metric, smooth, and completeness structures.
conclusion: Open: the catalog does not say whether the target defines structural stability or proves robustness, openness, a sufficient/necessary condition, a characterization, a classification, density, or existence.
degenerate_case_status: No case is excluded at intake because no proposition is selected; the statement phase must resolve every object, phase-space, time, regularity, perturbation, equivalence, locality, and boundary case listed below and in scope-map.md.
candidate_scope_not_credited: a source-specified definition asserting that every sufficiently small perturbation is topologically conjugate or orbit equivalent to the original system
a source-specified Andronov-Pontryagin result about rough planar autonomous systems and its exact necessary or sufficient conditions
a source-specified Peixoto theorem for vector fields on a compact two-dimensional manifold
a source-specified structural-stability theorem for hyperbolic sets, Anosov systems, Axiom A systems, or Morse-Smale systems
a local persistence or conjugacy theorem near a hyperbolic equilibrium or periodic orbit
degenerate_cases_to_resolve: empty, singleton, zero-dimensional, disconnected, noncompact, or boundary-bearing phase spaces
continuous versus discrete time and complete global flows versus maximal local solutions
vector fields versus their generated flows and maps versus diffeomorphisms
C0, C1, or Cr systems and the weak, strong, compact-open, Whitney, or another perturbation topology
global whole-space stability versus stability on a neighborhood, invariant set, orbit, or nonwandering set
topological conjugacy versus orbit equivalence and whether time parametrization may change
whether a conjugating homeomorphism must be close to the identity, isotopic to it, or preserve orientation
equilibria, periodic orbits, separatrices, nonhyperbolic points, and bifurcation-boundary systems
strict versus non-strict perturbation radii and the zero-perturbation boundary
excluded_substitutions: THM-M-1367 Peixoto's theorem or THM-M-1368 Morse-Smale systems
THM-M-1345 Hartman-Grobman, THM-M-1346 stable manifolds, or another local hyperbolic-equilibrium theorem
THM-M-1365 the Smale horseshoe, THM-M-1411 hyperbolic dynamical systems, or THM-M-1412 Anosov diffeomorphisms
a definition of structural stability projected from a structure that assumes the requested conjugacy or orbit equivalence
a scalar, linear, discrete, finite, or globally defined example used as the general theorem root
generic flow, homeomorphism, semiconjugacy, ODE, derivative, or topology APIs without an exact source-mapped theorem bridge
a numerical phase portrait, perturbation experiment, simulation, or empirical robustness test
the catalog's untrusted verified label, an attribution, a title match, or a discovery query used as proof evidence

freshness_and_revocation_policy: Invalidate on source or target correction, source/proposition selection, object or phase-space decision, regularity or perturbation topology, equivalence or time convention, neighbor-scope decision, Lean target or import, toolchain or dependency pin, assurance profile, validator, or any owned artifact change; independent review and master acceptance remain required.
status_boundary: Self-tested planned intake only. It freezes the catalog wording, duplicated source records, theorem-family choices, exclusions, neighbor boundaries, and adjacent pinned APIs. H5 classifies the received wording as an unstable proposition; it is not a claim that all valid structural-stability theorems are false or open. No canonical proposition, accepted source, exact Lean statement, proof body, H0, M0, R0, accepted execution state, audit completion, theorem completion, or master acceptance is claimed.
